_comment: One-shot DATA migrations: migrations whose purpose was to rewrite specific
business rows that existed on production at a specific moment. They are
schema-neutral — replaying them rebuilds no structure and no behavior.
They must never be replayed onto a database whose ledger does not already
contain them. Their authorization was bound to the live population at the
time they were written; a restored, staging, or drifted database is a
different population, and running the same UPDATE there rewrites rows
nobody approved. After a real restore the corrected values come back with
the DATA restore, not by re-running the edit.
from the replay plan and says so on stderr. --include-one-shot overrides it,
which is a deliberate, reviewed act, never a default.
Add an entry the moment a one-shot data migration is written. Schema and
function migrations do NOT belong here — they are idempotent by contract
and the replay plan must keep rebuilding them.

one_shot.20260810025159_backfill_stale_line_profi: Recomputed line-level profit for a 37-row population approved on 2026-08-09. Authorized by row/order/price counts, not by row identity — a different population with the same counts would satisfy that guard. Applied live; per AGENTS.md an applied migration is never edited, so containment lives here.
one_shot.20261007150100_mark_spring_2026_deliveri: Records 53 named spring 2026 deliveries on 33 orders as billed outside CRX (in Chem Man), owner-approved 2026-10-07. Bound to those live delivery and order numbers; on any other population its preflight refuses.
one_shot.20261007150200_release_reservations_of_d: Releases the reservations of four orders soft-deleted while still confirmed (4,607.1 units, 27 products) and of one deleted test order (36 units), owner-approved 2026-10-07. Bound to the live per-product reservation totals; its preflight refuses unless every product reconciles exactly.
